frequency_question: What proportion of Senate confirmation processes for major executive nominees are completed within 36 calendar days from initial submission?
membership_rule: Includes all Cabinet-level and major agency head (e.g., FDA, CDC, EPA) nominations submitted to the U.S. Senate since 2013 where a final floor vote occurred. Excludes nominations that were withdrawn or never brought to a vote before the end of a Congress.

cases.name: Marty Makary / current cycle hypothetical equivalents

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major FDA commissioner confirmation cycles examined; all exceeded 36 calendar days from formal submission to final floor vote due to mandatory ethics, background investigation, and committee notice periods.
known_gaps: Fast-tracked lower-level agency positions sometimes clear faster, but Senate-confirmed independent agency heads with statutory public health oversight consistently require 60-120 days minimum.
skeleton: Sequential mandatory procedural steps: nomination receipt (1 day), committee questionnaire and financial disclosures (14-21 days), background checks and ethics agreement (14-30 days), committee hearing scheduling and holding (14-21 days), committee reporting vote (7-14 days), floor scheduling and debate (7-14 days). Minimum theoretical sequential time sum is roughly 60 to 90 days under optimal conditions.
multiplier: Sum of minimum mandatory calendar days for background checks (14), ethics (14), committee notice/hearing (14), committee vote (7), and floor time (7) totals 56 calendar days minimum.
validity_reason: Senate procedural rules regarding committee notice periods, ethics reviews (OGE), and background checks (FBI) remain stable across Congresses unless major rule changes (like the nuclear option for lower courts) are applied, which do not alter the physical calendar constraints of document review.
